solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Order ambassador to infiltrate elite

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the ambassador's letters go within the word for elite

parts.note: the elite are the best
HE, His Excellency, is the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: A command tells an envoy to work his way into a privileged circle.
explanation.definitionFit: A behest is a command or instruction, as in 'at the king's behest', so it is a synonym of order.

clue.text: Risk only half improved

indicators.note: only half asks for just the front half of the word that follows

parts.note: improved means better

explanation.surface: A cautious gamble in which only half the hoped-for gains came true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps the first three of the six letters of BETTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To risk money on an outcome is to bet it, a verb-for-verb synonym.

clue.text: Expert's baking attempt

parts.note: baking weather is very hot
a shot is an attempt, as in 'have a shot'

explanation.surface: A star baker's go at a recipe, as on a TV cookery contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotshot is someone highly skilled and successful at something, an informal term for an ace.

clue.text: Kent town with management team providing promotional material

parts.note: Sandwich is a small historic town in the county of Kent
a company's board directs its management

explanation.surface: A company in a Kent town supplies advertising matter to clients.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent, a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandwich board is a pair of hinged advertising boards worn front and back by a walker in the street.

clue.text: Dozing snake has secured shelter

indicators.note: to secure here is to hold safely within, so the snake's letters wrap around the shelter

parts.note: an asp is a venomous snake
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind

explanation.surface: A sleeping serpent has found itself a cosy refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dozing is asleep, if only lightly, so the adjectives match.

clue.text: Boxing promoter, as it were — refuse to be handled by him?

definitions.meaning: a scrap is a fight, so someone dealing in scraps is jokingly a fight promoter

definitions.text: refuse to be handled by him?
definitions.meaning: a dealer in scrap metal handles what others throw away as refuse

explanation.surface: A fight promoter is so disreputable that one would decline to deal with him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' reads as a verb (decline) but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap merchant buys and sells discarded metal and other waste; scrap is also slang for a fight.

clue.text: Supply online joke?

parts.note: E, as in e-mail, stands for electronic or online
a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to provide an internet gag.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish them with what they need, a synonym of supply as a verb.

clue.text: Bird seen in separate line of hills

parts.note: to part is to separate
a ridge is a long narrow line of high ground

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher spots a game bird out on an isolated range of hills.
explanation.definitionFit: The partridge is a plump game bird of farmland, an example of a bird.

clue.text: Giant bird, and tailless

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird

indicators.note: tailless means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A huge bird that is also missing its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tailless' takes the D off AND, leaving AN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant gods of Greek myth, so a titan is any giant.

clue.text: Someone chasing a contented response, about to go to law

indicators.note: about means around, so the contented sound goes round the legal word

parts.note: a cat's purr is its contented response
to sue is to go to law against someone

explanation.surface: A pursuer, satisfied with an answer, is about to take legal action.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'about to' as 'on the point of'; in fact 'about' is the containment signal, wrapping the purr around the legal action.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuer is one who pursues, that is, someone chasing another.

clue.text: Sport in Post Office, behold!

parts.note: lo is an archaic word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Someone is amazed to find a game being played in a post office.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a team ball game played on horseback, an example of a sport.

clue.text: What you get from burning a tree

definitions.meaning: the powdery residue left after something burns

explanation.surface: A question about the result of setting fire to timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is both the residue of burning and the name of the tree genus Fraxinus.

clue.text: An old malicious heartless oddball

indicators.note: heartless means the central letters of the word are removed

explanation.surface: An elderly, spiteful, unfeeling eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' removes ICI from the middle of MALICIOUS, leaving MALOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective oddball means strange or irregular, which is what anomalous means.

clue.text: Monitor display with the whole thesis?

parts.note: all means the whole
an academic paper sets out a thesis

explanation.surface: A student puts a complete dissertation up on a computer screen.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallpaper is the background image shown on a computer monitor or phone screen.

clue.text: Make a choice: revolutionary science, visual science

parts.note: to opt is to make a choice

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A slogan urging people to choose radical science, then specifically that of sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests radical, but here it signals turning round the abbreviation for the first 'science'; the second 'science' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Optics is the branch of physics dealing with light and sight.

clue.text: Sailor drilling into stone floor of ocean

indicators.note: drilling into means boring inside, so the sailor goes within the stone

parts.note: the stone of a fruit is its seed
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A seaman bores into rock at the bottom of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The seabed is the ground at the bottom of the sea, the ocean's floor.

clue.text: Support son entering Bar with little hesitation

indicators.note: entering means going into, so the son's letter is placed within the bar

parts.note: a bolt is a bar used to fasten a door
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
er is a short sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A son walks into the pub, hesitating slightly, for some moral support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' suggests a pub or the legal profession, but it is a door bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: To bolster is to prop up or reinforce, a synonym of support as a verb.

clue.text: Horse farm's boss

definitions.meaning: an establishment where horses are bred
a boss, a raised knob such as on a shield or belt

explanation.surface: The manager of a stable for breeding horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boss' reads as manager but means a decorative knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud farm breeds horses; a boss is an ornamental round stud on a surface.

clue.text: Run out cricketer, one in a cricket club? Very agile

indicators.note: in places the run-out batsman and the one inside the club

parts.note: RO is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run out
a bat is a batsman, a cricketer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A batsman dismissed by a run-out wonders if he belongs in a cricket club.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batsman is 'run out' if the wicket is broken before he completes a run.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic describes the nimble gymnastic movement of an acrobat, so it means very agile.

clue.text: Weapon initially fired in anger

indicators.note: in shows the picked letter sits inside the word for anger

parts.note: to rile is to anger

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A gun was first discharged in a fit of rage.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled firearm, an example of a weapon.

clue.text: Fine to avoid long sentence — it's a complete fiction

indicators.note: to avoid means to leave out, so the fine's letter is dropped from the sentence

parts.note: a life sentence is the longest prison term
F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

explanation.surface: A criminal pays a fine to dodge a long jail term, which is a tall story.
explanation.definitionFit: A lie is an untrue statement, something entirely made up, a fiction.

clue.text: Casual worker appears after not working

indicators.note: appears after places the worker after the word for not working

parts.note: a machine that is off is not working
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A temp turns up once the machinery has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is casual or nonchalant, an adjective-for-adjective synonym.

clue.text: A cry of surprise about theatre's foremost performer

indicators.note: about means around, so the exclamation goes round the picked letter

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: foremost means take the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: An audience gasps at the leading player of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: COR, as in 'cor blimey', is a British informal cry of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor performs on stage or screen, so an actor is a type of performer.

clue.text: Ready to hide every other bit of sunlight

indicators.note: to hide every other letter means keeping only the alternate letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone prepares to block out alternating glimmers of sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A ray is a narrow beam of light, so a ray of sunlight is a bit of it.

clue.text: Regular small cuppa, duly emptied

parts.note: a cuppa is British slang for a cup of tea

indicators.note: emptied means the word's inner letters are removed, keeping only the outside ones

explanation.surface: A regular small cup of tea, properly drunk to the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Steady means constant and even, as in a steady pulse, a synonym of regular.

clue.text: Solid work at University perhaps involves Republican

indicators.note: involves means takes in, so the party letter sits inside the word for academic work

parts.note: to study is what one does at university, among other places

explanation.surface: Thorough academic research turns out to feature a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Sturdy means strongly built and robust, a synonym of solid.
